item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows a square of side $y-4$ split into four labelled regions.

Which expansion of $(y-4)^{2}$ is correct?

options.A: Call the result negative cross-products and treat that label alone as the expansion.
options.B: Writing $y^{2}-8y+16$ forces the original factor $(y-4)^{2}$ into place.
options.C: $(y-4)^{2}=(y-4)(y-4)=y^{2}-4y-4y+16=y^{2}-8y+16$, so the combined cross-term is negative.
options.D: $(y-4)^{2}=y^{2}-16$, as if the square were a plain difference of squares.
